# Standard deviation of columns and rows of large matrices

Produce the same result as `apply(x, 2, sd)` and `apply(x, 1, sd)`,
respectively. without coercing matrix to dense matrix. Values are not
identical to [`sd()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/sd.html) because of the
floating point precision issue in C++.

## Usage

``` r
colSds(x, use_nan = FALSE)

rowSds(x, use_nan = FALSE)
```

## Arguments

- x:

  a [base::matrix](https://rdrr.io/r/base/matrix.html) or
  [Matrix::Matrix](https://rdrr.io/pkg/Matrix/man/Matrix.html) object.

- use_nan:

  if `TRUE`, return `NaN` for columns or rows with all zero. Only used
  when `x` is a sparse matrix.

## Value

a numeric vector

## Examples

``` r
mt <- Matrix::rsparsematrix(100, 100, 0.9)
colSds(mt)
```
